verdict.rationale: Zep's governance docs describe authorization and audit controls on Context Graph operations. RBAC governs dashboard users, and ABAC policies attached to API keys and UserGroups limit which actions and context agents and Memory MCP users can reach (least-privilege). Audit Logs record dashboard activity and API Logs record API request activity. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration; explicit documentation of separate read vs. write permission rules; confirmation that API Logs cover all memory operations rather than only "supported" requests.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can govern who and what can read or write memory with roles, policies, or access-control lists, and audit that access

citations.quote: Zep applies authorization and audit controls to Context Graph operations. Role-based access control governs dashboard users.
Limit which actions and context each agent and Memory MCP user can reach with ABAC policies attached to API keys and UserGroups.
Use RBAC for humans. Use policies when you need least-privilege access to context for agents and Memory MCP users.
Audit Logs record dashboard activity, and API Logs record supported API request activity.
